One agent, every surface. Start a session on your desktop, steer it from your phone, pick it up in the terminal or drive it from your own code.

- [Desktop](https://opencode.ai/desktop): Sessions, tabs, diffs, built-in browser, and extensions on macOS, Windows and Linux.

### FAQ

#### What is OpenCode?

OpenCode is an open source agent that helps you write and run code with any AI model. It's available as a desktop app, a terminal interface, a mobile app and an SDK.

#### How do I use OpenCode?

The easiest way to get started is to read the [intro](https://opencode.ai/docs/).

#### Do I need extra AI subscriptions to use OpenCode?

Not necessarily. OpenCode comes with a set of free models that you can use without creating an account. You can even connect your [local models](https://opencode.ai/docs/models/#local). OpenCode also works with all popular providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI. [OpenCode Models](https://opencode.ai/console/models) give you access to popular coding models that we've tested and benchmarked for coding agents.

#### Can I use my existing AI subscriptions with OpenCode?

Yes, you can use your ChatGPT Plus/Pro or GitHub Copilot subscriptions. [Learn more](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/).

#### Can I only use OpenCode in the terminal?

No. OpenCode is also available as a [desktop app](https://opencode.ai/desktop) and a [mobile app](https://opencode.ai/mobile), and the [SDK](https://opencode.ai/sdk) lets you control it from your own code.

#### How much does OpenCode cost?

OpenCode is 100% free to use. It also comes with a set of free models. There might be additional costs if you connect any other provider.

#### What about data and privacy?

Your data and information is only stored when you use our free models. Learn more about [our models](https://opencode.ai/docs/console/models/#privacy).

#### Is OpenCode open source?

Yes, OpenCode is fully open source. The source code is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) under the [MIT License](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode?tab=MIT-1-ov-file#readme), meaning anyone can use, modify, or contribute to its development. # [Terminal](https://opencode.ai/terminal)

## Terminal

A fast terminal UI that works in any shell, editor or remote server. Describe what you want in plain words, watch each edit land as a diff, and choose which commands run on their own.

### Ask in plain words

Type what you want, and the agent shows its plan as it works.

### Approve what runs

Edits show as diffs, and commands wait for your permission.

### Make it yours

Switch themes in a keystroke, from the default to tokyonight and more.

### Mini

Run opencode mini and replies print into your own scrollback.

### Features

- **Any terminal:** Works in any shell, in your editor's terminal or on a remote server.
- **Diffs in the timeline:** See each edit as a diff in the timeline, as the agent makes it.
- **Pick up later:** Continue the last session with -c, or any with -s.
- **One-off runs:** opencode run sends one message and prints the reply.
- **Agents and commands:** Switch agents with shift+tab and open every command with ctrl+p.
- **Auto-approve:** Run with --auto to allow every action you haven't denied.

### About OpenCode

Descriptions of OpenCode and its products in long and short versions, ready to copy.

#### OpenCode

##### Long version

OpenCode is an open source coding agent. It comes as a desktop app, a terminal UI, a mobile app and an SDK, and it works with models from any provider, including Claude, GPT and Gemini. OpenCode is MIT licensed and made by Anomaly. It has over 220,000 GitHub stars and more than 1,000 contributors, and over 22 million developers use it every month.

##### Short version

OpenCode is an open source coding agent by Anomaly, with apps for desktop, the terminal and mobile, and an SDK.

#### OpenCode Console

##### Long version

OpenCode Console is the web app where developers and teams buy and manage AI model access for OpenCode and other coding agents. It offers pay-as-you-go inference for frontier and open-weight models, charged per request from prepaid credits, and OpenCode Go subscriptions. Teams get workspaces with Member, Admin and Owner roles, workspace and per-user spending limits, single sign-on with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or Google Workspace, and SCIM. Console supports more than 30 providers, so teams can connect provider accounts they already have, and its own inference is optional. It is at opencode.ai/console.

##### Short version

OpenCode Console is Anomaly's web app for pay-as-you-go AI model access, OpenCode Go subscriptions and team controls such as budgets and single sign-on.

#### OpenCode Go

##### Long version

OpenCode Go is a subscription for developers who want a fixed monthly price for coding models. Go costs $10/month, Go Plus costs $40/month with higher limits, and Go Teams costs $20/month per member. Each plan includes a curated set of models tested for agentic coding. Usage limits are monthly dollar amounts for each model, with rolling 5-hour and weekly allowances of 20% and 50% of the monthly limit. Subscribers can top up credit, fall back to a pay-as-you-go balance and cancel any time. Go works with OpenCode and other agents. It is at opencode.ai/console/go.

##### Short version

OpenCode Go is a monthly subscription from Anomaly that gives developers monthly usage limits on a curated set of coding models, from $10/month.

#### OpenCode Data

##### Long version

OpenCode Data is a public dashboard that shows which AI models developers use in OpenCode and how that mix changes over time. It publishes a leaderboard of top models, token usage, session and token costs, cache ratios, market share and a breakdown by country. The figures are aggregated every hour, with days and weeks in UTC. User and session counts are approximate, and costs use list prices from the OpenCode model catalog. Journalists can cite it as OpenCode Data (opencode.ai/data) with the update time shown on the page.

##### Short version

OpenCode Data is a public dashboard at opencode.ai/data that ranks AI models by real usage in OpenCode, with tokens, costs and market share updated hourly.

### Usage

Use the light versions on light backgrounds and the dark versions on dark backgrounds. The logo and the wordmark are separate, so use one or the other, never both together.

#### Clear space

Keep at least two strokes of space on every side of the logo and the wordmark. For the logo, a stroke is the thickness of its outline, a quarter of its width; for the wordmark, it is the thickness of its letters, a seventh of its height.

#### Whole pixels

The logo's proportions are fixed at 4:5, and one stroke is a quarter of its width. Scale it in steps of 4 × 5px, so every edge and every stroke lands on a whole pixel.

Logo sizes:
- 16 × 20px: 4px stroke
- 20 × 25px: 5px stroke
- 24 × 30px: 6px stroke
- 32 × 40px: 8px stroke
- 48 × 60px: 12px stroke
- 64 × 80px: 16px stroke

Wordmark sizes:
- 78 × 14px: 2px stroke
- 117 × 21px: 3px stroke
- 156 × 28px: 4px stroke
- 195 × 35px: 5px stroke
- 234 × 42px: 6px stroke
- 312 × 56px: 8px stroke

- **Do** keep every edge and the 4px stroke on whole pixels.
- **Do not** size the logo off 4:5, or its edges fall between pixels and blur.

#### Minimum sizes

- **Logo.** At least 16 × 20px, with a 4px stroke. Any smaller and it blurs.
- **Wordmark.** At least 117 × 21px, with a 3px stroke. Any smaller and it blurs.

Common mistakes to avoid when you use the logo and the wordmark.

- Do not recolor the logo in new colors.
- Do not use a single bright color.
- Do not fill the logo with a gradient.
- Do not swap the tones.
- Do not stretch or squash the logo.
- Do not add drop shadows.
- Do not add glows or outlines.
- Do not put other words next to the logo.
- Do not use low-contrast grey on grey.
- Do not put the grey two-tone logo on a colored background, where its greys turn muddy.

Put the OpenCode logo and the partner logo side by side, with a × between them. Leave 3 strokes of space on each side of the ×, size the partner logo to look as tall as the OpenCode logo, and keep clear space around the whole lockup.

#### Naming your project

Lead with your own name, so it is clear that the project is yours.

Write `Linear for OpenCode` or name the package `opencode-linear`. Do not write `OpenCode Linear` or `Linear by OpenCode`.

### Trademarks

OpenCode and the OpenCode logo are trademarks of Anomaly. Do not use them to suggest that Anomaly endorses or sponsors you, in your product or company name, or on merchandise without permission. For questions, email [press@anoma.ly](mailto:press@anoma.ly).

### Making it look like OpenCode

For agents that make a page, a slide, a document or an interface that should look like OpenCode. Partners who only use the logo can skip it.

#### Color

Use one grey scale. Each step has one job, the same in light and dark. Use no other greys, and no warm or tinted greys.

| Step | Job | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Page background | `#FBFBFB` | `#0C0C0C` |
| 2 | Cards, code blocks, panels, popovers | `#FFFFFF` | `#161616` |
| 3 | Subtle fill: inline code, search fields, bands | `#F5F5F5` | `#1A1A1A` |
| 4 | Hover fill, chips, selected tab | `#EEEEEE` | `#242424` |
| 5 | Borders and dividers | `#E0E0E0` | `#2E2E2E` |
| 6 | Strong borders and decoration | `#D2D2D2` | `#4B4B4B` |
| 7 | Icons and marks that carry meaning, disabled text | `#888888` | `#6A6A6A` |
| 8 | Muted text: captions, labels, meta | `#6B6B6B` | `#8F8F8F` |
| 9 | Body text | `#5C5C5C` | `#AEAEAE` |
| 10 | Emphasis text | `#3A3A3A` | `#DBDBDB` |
| 11 | Headings, strong text, the primary button | `#161616` | `#FAFAFA` |

- The dark background is `#0C0C0C` and the light background is `#FBFBFB`. Do not use pure black or pure white for a page.
- Cards and panels are lighter than the page in both themes.
- Text is at least 4.5:1 against its background, and icons and controls at least 3:1. Each step meets this when you use it for its job. On a hover fill (step 4), use step 8 or darker for text.
- Use steps 5 and 6 only for lines and decoration, never for text.
- The only accent is the link blue, `#3B5CF6` in light and `#6B8FFF` in dark. Use it for links, focus rings and selected or open states, not for decoration or large fills.
- The primary button is ink: step 11 with step 1 text. Text on the link blue is white.
- The logo colors above are for the logo and the wordmark only.
- No gradients, glows or drop shadows on text, and only soft, close shadows on raised surfaces.

#### Type

- Use OpenTUI Mono for headings, titles, navigation, labels and code, and Inter for body and reading text. Use no other fonts.
- Set headings in OpenTUI Mono at regular weight (400). Do not use bold for headings.
- Write labels and eyebrows in OpenTUI Mono, uppercase, at 12 to 14px, with a little letter spacing.
- Set body text in Inter at regular weight, 15 to 17px, with a line height of about 1.5. Keep lines to about 70 characters.
- Nothing is smaller than 12px. On phones, text that carries meaning is at least 14px.

#### Shape

- Use square corners. Round only avatars and dots (fully round), pills and app icons.
- Use one stroke weight for icons: 1.5px at 16px.
- Keep layouts on a grid, with plenty of space and hairline dividers (step 5) instead of boxes where you can.

#### Writing

- Write OpenCode as one word with a capital O and C. Call it an "open source coding agent".
- Write statements, not rhetorical questions, and use no colons in headings, buttons or captions.
- Write short, plain sentences.

# [Font](https://opencode.ai/font)

## OpenCode Font

A six-letter typeface cut from the OpenCode wordmark on a 4 × 7 grid. Type with it, see how every letter is built, then download your own installable font.

### Specimen

Six letters cut from the OpenCode wordmark. No curves, no diagonals, no exceptions: every edge falls on a grid of 120-unit modules.

### Construction

Each letter, rebuilt from nothing: the grid, the metrics, one module at a time, the shade, the outline, and the measurements that prove it.

### Timeline

The same construction as a schedule. Letters with more modules take longer to place; nothing else changes.

### Exploded view

Every module lifts by a stated rule: the order it was placed, its row, or its distance from the centre. Equal steps stay equal.

### Glyph passports

One page per letter: identity, measurements and every point of its outline in font units.

### Analysis

Ink, counters, symmetry and the 28 positions of the grid, counted across all six letters.

### Kerning

Thirty-six pairs. Every one of them spaced by the same 120 units. The kerning table is empty, and that is the point.

### Performance

A font small enough to read in one sitting.

### Anagrams

The letters of opencode can be arranged 10,080 ways. Try them all.

### Field

A field of the six letters.

### Loupe

Look closer. Every module of every letter is a grid of 144 smaller squares.

### Tester

Type with the six letters. Other characters stay empty.

### Colophon

Download the font, install it, then choose OpenCode in any app. Every copy carries its own substitution map.

We store this so the agent can finish its work and continue the conversation later. We delete a session and its sandbox 30 days after its last activity, such as a message to the agent, a scheduled run or a response it finishes. Reading a session doesn't count as activity. We delete them sooner when the agent, its service account or the workspace is deleted. We also delete them sooner when the Slack, GitHub or email inbox connection the session came through is disconnected or removed, such as by uninstalling OpenCode from Slack, or when the agent no longer has a trigger (the setting that lets a Slack workspace, Discord server, GitHub repository, inbox, webhook or schedule start the agent) for the place the session came from. While the inbox is connected, we keep each email's sender, recipient, subject and a preview of up to 200 characters, along with the agent's draft and sent replies and its notes to your team, in the workspace's review queue, and delete them after the inbox is disconnected or the workspace is deleted. If someone schedules a task with the agent in Slack, we keep its instructions until 30 days after the schedule ends, or until Slack is disconnected or the workspace is deleted. To ask us to delete a session or email thread sooner, email [help@anoma.ly](mailto:help@anoma.ly).

#### Product Analytics on opencode.ai

When you visit opencode.ai, including the docs and the Console, we record the pages you view, how long each page is visible, how long you're active on it, how far you scroll and how quickly it loads. We also record the links and buttons you click, when you download an app or copy a command, when you search (but not what you search for), and the type of any sign-in error. We record each click under a fixed name we give that link or button, so text you or your team entered, such as workspace names or email addresses, isn't recorded even when it appears on the page. We record account and workspace events: when you sign up, sign in, verify your email, approve a device, create or delete a workspace, invite or remove members, create API keys, connect providers or clients, and start or complete a checkout or payment, including its amount and any decline reason. We use these records to understand how people find OpenCode and where they stop before signing up or subscribing, so we can improve the Services.

We collect these records ourselves and don't use third-party analytics services on opencode.ai.

With each record sent from your browser, we keep the country, region and time zone your request came from, the type of device, operating system and browser you used, and the size of your browser window. We use your IP address to determine your country and region and to limit requests, but we don't store it, your email address or anything you type in these records.

We set the following first-party Cookies. Your browser sends them only to opencode.ai. We also keep a list in your browser's local storage of which events it has already reported that day.

| Cookie | What it holds | How long it lasts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| oc_vid | A random ID for your browser | 1 year from your latest visit |
| oc_sid | An ID for your current visit and the time it started | 30 minutes without activity, and at most 24 hours |
| oc_attr | The page you first and most recently landed on, the domain of the website that referred you and any campaign (UTM) parameters in the link, plus the last link into the Console you clicked (a sign-up or sign-in link, and the plan it was for, if any) and when you clicked it | 1 year from the last time it changed |
| oc_optout | A record that you turned off analytics in this browser | 1 year from your latest visit |

When you create an account, sign in, verify your email or approve a device, we link the records from that browser to your account. Records made while you're signed in carry your account ID directly.

If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control signal, or you [turn off analytics on this page](https://opencode.ai/legal/privacy-policy#product-analytics), we still record the page views, clicks and other browser events above, but without the IDs and arrival details in oc_vid, oc_sid and oc_attr, and without your account or workspace ID. We delete those Cookies and the local storage list from your browser and don't set them again while analytics are off. Account and workspace events, such as sign-ups, payments and workspace changes, still carry your account ID, but we don't link them or any other records to that browser, even if you're signed in.

We delete these records from our analytics database within a month after they turn 24 months old. We keep an archive copy of these records for longer. It contains your account ID if you were signed in, but not your name, email address or IP address. When you delete your account, we delete your email address, our record of how you first arrived and our list of the browsers linked to your account. Event records that include your account ID, and the browser IDs recorded with them, remain until they're deleted at 24 months, and in the archive, but we can no longer connect that account ID to you.
